title: Protocol for the sonogenetic stimulation of mouse brain by non-invasive ultrasound
protocol: Setup the ultrasound system.
Make a water tube.
Prepare a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Shorten the sharp side of the tube until the diameter of the aperture is 6 mm.
Shorten the tube until it is 4 cm long.
Seal the aperture with plastic wrap (Sinya).
Fix the plastic wrap with sealing film.
Fill the prepared tube with water that has been standing more than 12 hours, to reduce air bubbles.
Pour water carefully into the tube to minimize formation of new air bubbles.
Affix the water-filled tube to the 500 kHz transducer slowly to avoid air gaps or bubbles between the transducer and water.
Dry any overflowing water with tissue.
Fix the transducer to the water tube using sealing film.
Screw the integrated ultrasound transducer onto a stand.
Connect the output of the function generator to the input of the power amplifier with BNC wiring.
Connect the output of the power amplifier to the transducer.
Anesthetize the mouse with ketamine and xylazine via IP injection with a disposable syringe.
Judge the level of anesthesia by tail and foot pinch reflexes.
Confirm that the mouse is deeply anesthetized before proceeding.
Place ointment on the mouse’s eyes to prevent drying during the procedure.
Shave the fur around the skull.
Sterilize the shaved regions with 70% alcohol.
Pad the mouse's lower jaw with paper towels to ensure a flat head position.
Use 70% alcohol to sterilize the shaved region again.
Centrifuge the ultrasound gel at 1000 g for 10 min before doing the experiment.
Put some ultrasound gel on the surface of the shaved region.
Make sure air bubbles are not present in the gel.
Place the ultrasound transducer on the surface of the ultrasound gel atop the targeted regions.
Ensure the distance between the water tube and the surface of the mouse brain is around 2 mm.
Position the middle of the transducer on the injection site.
Stimulate the mouse with ultrasound (500 kHz, 400 μs pulse width, 1 ms pulse interval, 300 ms stimulation duration, and 0.3 MPa) for 40 min with a 10 s inter-stimulus interval.
After stimulation, return the mouse to its original cage.
Perfuse the mouse with PBS 90 minutes after ultrasound treatment.
Follow this by perfusing the mouse with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.
Keep the isolated brain in 4% PFA for 12-16 hours at 4°C.
Wash the brain with 1×PBS three times, each for 15 minutes.
Prepare vibratome slices of the brain spaced 40 μm apart.
Fill the vibratome chamber with PBS.
Attach the perfused brain to the pad using superglue.
After each slice, place it in an individual well filled with PBS.
Block the slices in blocking buffer (10% normal goat serum + 5% BSA + 0.3% Triton in 1×PBS) for 2 hours at 22°C–24°C.
Incubate slices with primary antibody (dilution 1:500; Cell Signaling Technology, 2250) diluted in blocking buffer for 16-20 hours at 4°C.
Wash the slices with 1×PBS three times, each for 5 minutes.
Incubate slices with secondary antibody (goat anti-rabbit IgG, Alexa Fluor 555; Invitrogen, dilution 1:1,000) diluted in blocking buffer for 2 hours at 22°C–24°C.
Wash slices for 5 min three times.
Remove the brain slice from storage and place on the glass slide with a brush or other thin utensil.
Let the slide dry for 5 min.
Administer small drops of Prolong Diamond Antifade Mountant with DAPI.
Place cover slide on top of the glass slide.
Image the brain slices using a confocal microscope (TCS SP8, Leica).
Count c-Fos signals using ImageJ.
Set up the EMG and ultrasound system.
Connect the ultrasound system to the EMG system for synchronization.
Hold the mouse in the procedure room for 30 min before beginning the experiment.
Anesthetize the mouse with 2% isoflurane for 5 min in the isoflurane box.
Place the mouse flat on the operation table.
Spread all four limbs to ensure easy accessibility.
Connect a tube that outputs isoflurane and oxygen to the mouse’s nose.
Maintain consistent isoflurane concentration throughout the experiment.
Add a 37°C heating pad under the mouse’s body during the entire procedure if necessary.
Consistently check on the mouse’s condition by observing its heartbeat.
If the vitals are weak, decrease the isoflurane concentration.
Place ointment on the mouse’s eyes to prevent drying.
Shave the fur on the mouse’s head and around the left forelimb near the triceps muscle carefully.
Disinfect the surgical region with 70% alcohol, moving outwards from the middle of the surgical site.
Take the scalpel and blunt forceps.
Use the blunt forceps to gently hold the exposed skin on the left forelimb and make an incision with the scalpel.
Separate two sides of skin with cotton tip slightly to expose the triceps.
Clean the blood with a cotton tip.
Insert two recording electrodes into the triceps 2 mm deep and leave 2–3 mm between the electrodes.
Fix the electrodes with a sticker.
Connect a ground electrode to the tail.
Apply some ultrasound gel on the top of the mouse’s head.
Make sure no air bubbles are present in the gel.
Place the integrated ultrasound transducer mentioned above on the mouse’s head, with the middle of transducer on the injection site.
Setup the ultrasound system with the following parameters: 500 kHz frequency, 400 μs pulse width, 1 ms pulse interval, 300 ms stimulation duration, 5 s interval.
Reduce the concentration of isoflurane to 0.5%–0.8%.
Allow the mice to rest for 5 min to adapt to the new level of isoflurane.
Open the EMG software.
Press the input button and check that the EMG signal is present.
Press the record button and name the file.
Record 1 min of the EMG signal without ultrasound stimulation.
Adjust the amplitude of ultrasound to 0.05 MPa.
Press the start button in the ultrasound machine.
Treat the mouse with 0.05 MPa ultrasound stimulation for 7–10 times.
Press the stop button after ultrasound stimulation.
Rest for around 60 s.
Repeat steps for the other acoustic pressure.
Press the stop button in the EMG recording software after all acoustic pressures are tested.
Adjust the concentration of isoflurane to 2% for 2 min to reduce pain during electrode withdrawal.
Remove the recording electrodes from the triceps with tweezers and remove the ground wire from the mouse’s tail.
Use an alcohol-soaked cotton tip to disinfect the triceps.
Prepare the sterile suture and needle and clamp the needle with a needle holder.
Gently push the suture into the skin and use blunt forceps to grasp the skin on the other side of the incision.
Pull the suture material out until approximately 0.75 inches remain and make a knot.
Repeat the suture step 3–5 times or until the incision is fully closed.
Use an interrupted knot.
Continue to warm the mouse with the heater until the mouse wakes up.
Place the mouse into the original cage.
